result.rationale: The diff explicitly skips the sanitizing cook pipeline: post.rb's cook returns raw when cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html], TopicEmbed.import sets that cook_method for remote feed/retrieved content (via import_remote using ruby-readability), and best.html.erb renders it via `raw post.cooked`. Since only embeddable_host is checked (not content sanitization), a malicious or compromised embedded site's HTML executes in the Discourse-origin iframe. This is a security defect grounded directly in the diff.

judged_text: TopicEmbed.import stores remote feed/retrieved HTML as cooked content with cook_method raw_html, bypassing the sanitizing cook pipeline, and best.html.erb renders it with raw post.cooked, so any script/iframe injected into the source RSS feed or embedded page executes in the Discourse-origin embed iframe. A compromised or malicious embedded site feeds arbitrary HTML through import_remote/PollFeed; it is rendered unsanitized at /embed/best, giving an attacker script execution in the forum's origin (cookie/CSRF theft) — the normal cook pipeline's sanitization is the control this diff explicitly skips.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly introduces a `cook_method` of `:raw_html` (Post.cook_methods) and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, bypassing the normal cooking/rendering pipeline (which is typically where sanitization would occur). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and supplies HTML content from RSS (`Jobs::PollFeed` uses `i.content`/`CGI.unescapeHTML`) or remote fetch (`TopicEmbed.import_remote` uses `open(url).read`). The embed view `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` renders `raw post.cooked`, so any HTML stored will be emitted unescaped into `/embed/best` under the Discourse origin. This makes injection of `<script>`/dangerous HTML from the feed/remote page a real XSS risk in the embedded iframe, consistent with the finding.
